conviction_note: Session resolved: the Q2 call is 9:00 P.M. ET on 2026-08-31, so the release is after today's close and the reaction lands in the 2026-09-01 session (amc confirmed). Direction is negative because Q2 (Apr-Jun) is the quarter in which Cango's own disclosed cash cost per BTC ($68,061 in April) sat above the prevailing BTC price (~$63k through June), production had already fallen ~45% versus Q1 on the two monthly updates that were published, and the company then went dark on monthly operational disclosure for 82 days -- all of it landing on a stock that is +43.7% in 20 days and +65% off a 52-week low set three weeks ago purely on BTC beta. Magnitude is held to -3.5 rather than double digits because the comparable Q1 disaster print (revenue -43% q/q, -$261m net loss, 2026-06-01) produced roughly a zero move in the baseline's own history, i.e. the marginal holder of this name does not trade it on the P&L, and because an EcoHash customer or GPU-contract announcement bundled with the release is a live fat right tail.

findings.finding: Cango has published no monthly operational / bitcoin-production update since 2026-06-10 (May data): its own newsroom shows nothing between the 2026-06-24 EGM result and the 2026-08-25 earnings-date notice, so June, July and August updates are all missing -- an 82-day gap against a monthly cadence the company had held since at least mid-2025, and while peer Canaan kept publishing (June update on 2026-07-14). The market's last hashrate/production/treasury data point is therefore 31.67 EH/s, 237.59 BTC and 1,065.11 BTC as of 2026-05-31, and tonight's release supplies the June number nobody has.
findings.why_not_priced: A search specifically for commentary on Cango discontinuing its monthly production disclosure returns nothing -- not Blockspace, not TheMiningMag, not Hashrate Index, all of which cover Cango. If it were priced you would see the sector trackers flagging stale data and you would not see the stock +43.7% in 20 days; instead ziven.io (formerly bitcoinminingstock.io) is still serving 31 May 2026 operational metrics next to a 31 Aug 2026 price stamp with no staleness warning, which is what a market that has not noticed looks like. A miner that stops publishing the metric its equity story rests on, in the exact months when its own disclosed cash cost sat above spot BTC, is not usually withholding good news.
findings.independence: Independently corroborated by two other sources with no shared feed: EDGAR shows no 6-K filed between 2026-07-21 and today (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001725123.json), and stocktitan's CANG news list jumps from the 06/10 May update straight to the 07/10 consolidation notice (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CANG/). Directionally supported by Antalpha's 2026-08-19 Q2 report showing mining supply-chain financing TVL down 46% q/q to $384m, i.e. a violent Q2 contraction across the miner complex (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ANTA/antalpha-reports-second-quarter-2026-aaapadu4dgce.html).

findings.finding: Cango's own April 2026 release disclosed an average cash cost of $68,061 per coin, while BTC traded around $62,953-$63,400 through June 2026 -- so Cango self-mined at a negative cash margin for most of the quarter being reported, on a cash balance of $7.2m at 31 March (down from $41.2m at year-end) and with Q2 self-mined production of only 466.5 BTC in April+May against 1,266.1 BTC in the whole of Q1.
findings.why_not_priced: The crossover requires joining three documents that no aggregator joins: Cango's April cost-per-coin, the June BTC price, and the Q1 cash balance from the transcript rather than the press release. stockanalysis.com lists analyst coverage as 'n/a' and no price target for CANG, there is no options market at all per the baseline, and market cap is $96m on 41.0m shares -- there is nobody on the sell side doing this arithmetic. If it were priced, the stock would not have re-rated 65% off a $1.36-1.40 52-week low set in early August while the quarter being reported was the worst mining-economics quarter in the company's history.
findings.independence: Cash position and Q1 production from the Q1 transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/02/cango-cang-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/, 2026-06-02: $7.2m cash, 1,266.1 BTC mined at $76,928 cash cost). BTC-below-production-cost for five straight months independently from JPMorgan via https://www.spendnode.io/blog/jpmorgan-bitcoin-below-production-cost-five-months-june-2026/. Overlaps with finding 1 -- the same quarter, seen from the cost side rather than the disclosure side.

findings.finding: The AI pivot that carries the equity story is, on inspection of the company's own live product site, a small self-serve GPU cloud: ecohash.com sells single-to-8-GPU instances of NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 (96GB Blackwell) workstation cards, LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning on 1-4 GPUs, an OpenAI-compatible inference API from $0.02/1M tokens, and a $1 free credit on signup, with no customer logos or case studies. Management guided on the Q1 call only that 'revenue generation will start in the second half of this year' with no targets.
findings.why_not_priced: The coverage of EcoHash (Forbes 2026-07-08, DataCenterDynamics, the 2026-04-13 launch release) describes the strategy -- distributed inference at 10-50MW sites instead of hyperscaler training campuses -- and never the SKU. Nobody has published what is actually for sale. If the market had priced the gap between 'HPC and AI inference subsidiary of a 31 EH/s miner' and 'RTX Pro 6000 rentals with a $1 signup credit', the stock would not be trading a BTC-pivot-to-AI multiple. This is the one finding with a genuine right tail: an earnings release is exactly where a first EcoHash contract would be bundled, and that would invert the sign.
findings.independence: Guidance language from the Q1 transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/02/cango-cang-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/, 2026-06-02). Strategy framing, which the site contradicts in scale, from https://www.forbes.com/sites/boazsobrado/2026/07/08/what-not-to-do-a-bitcoin-miner-bets-against-ais-giant-data-centers/. Independent of findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: Today's close is the mechanical NYSE compliance test and it passes. The 2026-03-10 NYSE deficiency notice gave a six-month cure period expiring around 2026-09-10, curable only 'on the last trading day of any calendar month during the Cure Period' with both a $1.00 close and a $1.00 average close over the trailing 30 trading days. 31 August is the last month-end inside that window, and it is exactly the 30th trading day since the 10-for-1 consolidation took effect on 21 July (9 July sessions + 21 August sessions, no intervening holiday) -- so this is the first and last month-end on which the whole lookback is post-consolidation tape. At $2.27-2.41 today and a 52-week low of $1.36, both prongs clear.
findings.why_not_priced: The date arithmetic -- that the cure clock runs out around 10 September, that 31 August is the only remaining qualifying month-end, and that the post-split trading-day count hits exactly 30 today -- appears nowhere in the coverage, which stops at 'Cango warned by NYSE, six months to comply'. No aggregator carries cure-period expiry dates. If it were priced, the run-up would show a company-specific kink; instead the 43.7% 20-day move maps cleanly onto BTC going from ~$63k to ~$78k in August, so the rally is beta and contains no compliance premium. A 'regained compliance' release should follow within days and removes a delisting tail that keeps institutional money out of the name.
findings.independence: Cure-period mechanics and the deficiency date corroborated by https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/CANG/pressreleases/1133318/cango-warned-by-nyse-over-sub1-share-price-given-six-months-to-regain-compliance/. Consolidation effective date 2026-07-20/21 from https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cango-inc-announces-effective-date-and-ratio-for-share-consolidation-302822530.html. Cuts against findings 1-3.

findings.finding: Antalpha's Q2 2026 report -- filed 2026-08-19, i.e. after Cango last spoke and reporting on the same 30 June balance-sheet date -- states that revenue excluding 'the Cango facility repaid in the first quarter of 2026' was $11.6m, that technology financing fees fell 40% y/y 'primarily reflecting the wind-down of the Cango facility', and that Antalpha has recorded no principal loss since inception. That is the counterparty confirming, from the other side of the ledger, that Cango's bitcoin-collateralised borrowing is fully extinguished with no credit event -- which implies the $68.2m of 'Bitcoin collateral receivables' on Cango's 31 March balance sheet releases into unencumbered BTC during Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing links the two tickers. Cango's 2025 20-F flags Antalpha related-party loans of $557.6m as roughly 50% of total assets and margin-call/forced-sale risk as its top financing risk; the resolution of that risk was disclosed by Antalpha, in Antalpha's release, 12 days ago, to Antalpha's shareholders. If the market had read it across, the residual counterparty-default discount in CANG would have compressed on 19-20 August, which it did not -- CANG's August path tracks BTC, not ANTA's print day. Note the same document carries a bearish read for finding 1 (mining supply-chain financing TVL -46% q/q to $384m).
findings.independence: Cango side of the same fact from the Q1 transcript (long-term debt $30.6m from $557.6m; $68.2m Bitcoin collateral receivable) at https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/02/cango-cang-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/, 2026-06-02, and the 20-F risk framing at https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CANG/20-f-cango-inc-files-annual-report-foreign-issuer-b60e59403207.html. baseline_tension: SESSION RESOLVED, NOT AS THE CALENDAR HAS IT IN SPIRIT: the 2026-08-25 notice pairs the release with a 9:00 P.M. ET conference call, so the release is post-close on 31 August and the reaction is the 1 September session -- amc is right, but for a Beijing-morning audience, which is part of why the comparable Q1 print moved this stock roughly zero. The baseline's own numbers are the thing my finding has to beat and mostly they do not describe it: there is no options market, so no skew and no priced direction at all, and the eight 'reactions' are monthly production 6-Ks, not prints. What the baseline does say is the +43.73% 20-day run-up and +65.29% off the 52-week low, and my findings cut hard against it -- that entire rally maps onto BTC moving from ~$63k to ~$78k in August (CNBC, 2026-08-21; Fortune, 2026-08-30) and contains no company-specific good news, while the quarter being reported is precisely the one in which Cango mined below its own cash cost, produced ~45% less than Q1, and stopped telling anyone what its hashrate was. So the run-up is the vulnerability rather than a warning that I am late. Against that, two things pull positive and I have sized them positive rather than argued them away: BTC at $78k puts Cango's forward cash margin around +$10k/coin for the first time in five months, and the NYSE cure period is cleared by today's close. Net -3.5, capped well inside the 175% realised vol (~11% daily sigma) because a bundled EcoHash contract announcement is a real right tail.
